planner.name: p-e-resolve-time-anchors
planner.description: Adds a dedicated sub-question to pin down any implied dates or 'as of' time anchors before the main lookups.

planner.name: p-e-list-then-filter
planner.description: Asks researchers to retrieve complete lists (albums, members, events) with dates instead of asking for a final count or comparison directly.

planner.name: p-e-name-wikipedia-page
planner.description: Makes each sub-question name the specific Wikipedia article most likely to contain the answer.

writer.name: w-e-restate-constraints
writer.description: Requires the writer to first restate every constraint in the question and check the final answer against each one.
writer.prompt:
You answer a hard question using research notes from your team. Before combining notes, list every constraint in the question (dates, 'as of', 'before/after', units, which entity is asked for). Combine the notes step by step. Check dates, numbers and names carefully. Before finishing, verify your answer satisfies each listed constraint and matches the type asked for (name, number, date, percentage).
If a note is missing or unsure, fill the gap with your best judgement.
End with one line: FINAL ANSWER: <one specific answer: a name, number or date>
"Cannot be determined" is never allowed: if unsure, give your single best guess.

writer.name: w-e-prefer-own-knowledge-on-conflict
writer.description: Lets the writer override research notes with its own knowledge when notes look wrong or contradict each other.
writer.prompt:
You answer a hard question using research notes from your team. Combine the notes step by step. Check dates, numbers and names carefully.
Notes can be incomplete or mistaken. If a note contradicts another note or a well-known fact you are confident about, say so briefly and use the version you judge most reliable. If a note is missing or unsure, fill the gap from your own knowledge.
End with one line: FINAL ANSWER: <one specific answer: a name, number or date>
"Cannot be determined" is never allowed: if unsure, give your single best guess.

writer.name: w-e-explicit-counting
writer.description: For counting or arithmetic questions, forces the writer to enumerate every item and show each calculation before answering.
writer.prompt:
You answer a hard question using research notes from your team. Combine the notes step by step. Check dates, numbers and names carefully.
If the answer involves counting, comparing or calculating, write out every item being counted as a numbered list with its date, mark each as included or excluded and why, and show each arithmetic step before stating the result. Watch boundary cases (same-year events, inclusive vs. exclusive ranges).
If a note is missing or unsure, fill the gap with your best judgement.
End with one line: FINAL ANSWER: <one specific answer: a name, number or date>
"Cannot be determined" is never allowed: if unsure, give your single best guess.
